//: Advisories the dependency audit is allowed to ignore, and only until the date
on each entry. Every field is required and every one is enforced by
id       the GHSA or CVE identifier, or the package name for an advisory
reason   why shipping with it is acceptable. 'not exploitable here' is not
a reason; say which code path is or is not reached.
expires  ISO date. ON AND AFTER THIS DATE THE BUILD FAILS, whether or not
the advisory is still open. An allowlist that never expires is a
permanent exception with a comment attached, which is how a known
vulnerability becomes a forgotten one. Renewing an entry is a
deliberate act with a fresh reason.
Four entries today, all of them the same finding: the console's build and
test toolchain (vite 5, vitest 2) carries advisories that are only fixed by
moving to vite 7 and vitest 3. That upgrade hit a peer dependency conflict
with @vitejs/plugin-react and is a migration of its own, not a line in a
security commit. The expiry is deliberately short so it comes back.

allow.reason: vitest UI server reads and executes arbitrary files. The UI server is never started: CI runs `vitest run` and no script in this repo passes --ui. Test tooling only, not reachable from any shipped package or from the gateway. Fix requires vitest 3.

vite dev server path traversal in optimized deps .map handling. The dev server runs only on a developer machine via `npm run dev`; the console is shipped as a static build and no deployment serves vite. Fix requires vite 7.

launch-editor NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC paths on Windows, reached only through the vite dev server error overlay. Same exposure as above: dev only, and no Windows developer or CI runner is in use. Fix requires vite 7.
vite server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths. Dev server only, and nothing in this repo runs a vite server outside a developer machine. Fix requires vite 7.
